response.sql: SELECT o.orderflow AS status, AVG(NULLIF(e.fillcount, 0)) AS avg_fillcount, COUNT(*) AS execution_count, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS execution_fraction FROM orders o JOIN orderexecutions e ON e.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.orderflow;

assumptions.assumption: execution_count counts every execution linked to an order, including executions with a missing or zero fillcount. The 'left out' clause is read as applying only to the average, not the count.
The fraction's denominator is the total of execution_count across all statuses, so the fractions sum to 1 over the joined executions. Executions with no matching order are excluded by the inner join.
Orders with a NULL orderflow form their own NULL status group rather than being dropped.

alternatives.interpretation: Zero and missing fills are excluded from the count as well as the average, so execution_count and the fraction only cover executions with a non-zero, non-null fillcount.
alternatives.sql: SELECT o.orderflow AS status, AVG(NULLIF(e.fillcount, 0)) AS avg_fillcount, COUNT(NULLIF(e.fillcount, 0)) AS execution_count, CAST(COUNT(NULLIF(e.fillcount, 0)) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(NULLIF(e.fillcount, 0))) OVER () AS execution_fraction FROM orders o JOIN orderexecutions e ON e.ordersmark = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.orderflow;
